source.title: Troubleshoot failed requests by using tracing in IIS

stage.title: HTTP.sys to IIS
stage.description: The request is accepted by HTTP.sys and handed to the IIS worker process.

stage.title: Begin request
stage.description: Native and managed modules can inspect or reject the request before authentication.

stage.title: Authenticate
stage.description: Authentication modules establish the request identity.

stage.title: Authorize
stage.description: Authorization modules decide whether the established identity can access the resource.

stage.title: Resolve cache
stage.description: IIS and application caches can satisfy the request before handler execution.

stage.title: Map handler
stage.description: IIS selects the handler responsible for the requested resource.

stage.title: Acquire state
stage.description: Application state and session-related modules prepare request state.

stage.title: Execute handler
stage.description: The selected native, managed, FastCGI, or ASP.NET Core handler processes the request.

stage.title: Release state
stage.description: Request state is persisted or released after handler execution.

stage.title: Update cache
stage.description: Eligible responses can update IIS or application caches.

stage.title: End request
stage.description: Final response processing completes and the request leaves the pipeline.

rule.definition: IIS IP Address and Domain Restrictions rejected the client before authentication and handler execution.

causes.cause: The client IP is denied by an explicit allow or deny rule.
A reverse proxy address is evaluated instead of the intended client address.
The effective site or application configuration inherits a restriction from a parent scope.

actions.action: Review the effective ipSecurity configuration at server, site, application, and path scope.
Confirm which address IIS evaluated and validate trusted proxy and forwarded-address behavior.
Change allow or deny rules only after confirming the blocked address is expected traffic.

rule.definition: IIS Request Filtering rejected the URL, verb, extension, sequence, header, or request size.

causes.cause: A requestFiltering rule blocks the requested pattern.
The request exceeds configured content or URL limits.

actions.action: Use the HTTP substatus and FREB event data to identify the exact filtering rule.
Prefer the narrowest safe configuration change and retest the same request.

rule.definition: An IIS authentication module could not establish or accept the request identity.

causes.cause: The enabled authentication providers do not match the client and application requirements.
Credentials, SPNs, delegation, or provider order are incorrect.

actions.action: Correlate the HTTP substatus, Windows security events, and the selected authentication providers.
Verify identity and delegation changes in a controlled environment before production rollout.

rule.definition: Authorization denied an authenticated or anonymous identity access to the resource.

causes.cause: URL authorization, NTFS permissions, or application authorization rules deny the identity.

actions.action: Identify the effective identity, then review URL authorization and filesystem permissions separately.

rule.definition: IIS could not load or validate the effective configuration for the request.

causes.cause: The configuration contains invalid XML, an unrecognized section, a locked section, or inaccessible configuration data.

actions.action: Use the HRESULT and configuration path in the FREB event to locate the failing file and setting.
Check section locking, schema availability, file permissions, and duplicate declarations.

rule.definition: ASP.NET Core Module could not start, load, or communicate with the hosted application.

causes.cause: The application failed during startup, the runtime is missing, or hosting configuration is invalid.

actions.action: Correlate the exact substatus with ANCM Event Viewer and stdout evidence.
Verify the deployed runtime, processPath, arguments, hosting model, and application startup logs.

rule.definition: The selected request handler failed while processing the application request.

causes.cause: Application code, a native extension, FastCGI, ASP.NET, or another handler returned an error.

actions.action: Use the failing module, HRESULT, and neighboring trace events to select the matching application or runtime logs.
Do not treat the final HTTP status alone as proof of the application root cause.
